content: Start with the default cube, give it a Geometry Nodes Modifier, and then set up the network with an [k]Ico Sphere[/k] and [k]Dual Mesh[/k] (Image 1). The [k]Dual Mesh[/k] node converts a mesh into its dual, i.e. faces are turned into vertices and vertices are turned into faces (Image 2). Using this node gives our sphere a better shape for our asteroid. Add in an [k]Extrude Mesh[/k] node and set the Offset very low (Image 3). The [k]Extrude Mesh[/k] node generates new edges or faces on the selected geometry elements and moves them by a certain offset. Add a [k]Scale Elements[/k] node, and make its selection the Top output of the [k]Extrude Mesh[/k] (Image 4).
The [i]Extrude Mesh Node[/i] generates new edges or faces on the selected geometry elements and moves them by a certain offset.

The operations are similar to the extrude tools in mesh edit mode, though there are some differences. Most importantly, the node never keeps the back-faces of the extrusion in place, they are always removed. Attribute propagation rules may also be different.
A boolean field indicating the “top” elements in the extrusion. In [i]Vertex[/i] mode, these are the new vertices; in [i]Edge[/i] mode, the new edges; and in [i]Face[/i] mode, the moved faces.

A boolean field indicating the “side” elements in the extrusion. In [i]Vertex[/i] mode, these are the new edges; in [i]Edge[/i] mode, the new faces; and in [i]Face[/i] mode, too, the newly generated faces (as opposed to the moved ones).

Add a [k]Scale Elements[/k] node, and make its selection the Top output of the [k]Extrude Mesh[/k] (Image 4). [k]Shift-D[/k] the [k]Extrude Mesh[/k] node and extrude after the scaling, but limit the extrusion just to the Top elements of the first extrusion (Image 5). Change the Offset Scale of the second [k]Extrude Mesh[/k] so that the faces extrude inwards (Image 6). Duplicate the [k]Scale Elements[/k] node and connect it to the network, using it to scale in the indentations we made (Image 7). Add in a [k]Subdivision Surface[/k] node, increase the Level, and add a [k]Set Shade Smooth[/k] node (Image 8).

We will start varying the shape by adding some [k]Random Value[/k] nodes. The first [k]Random Value[/k] node will be used to randomize the Offset Scale applied to the first [k]Extrude Mesh[/k] node and the second [k]Random Value[/k] node will randomize the scale applied to the Top faces (Image 9). Next, we will randomize how many sides get extruded into craters; add a [k]Random Value[/k] node, attach it to the Selection input for the first [k]Extrude Mesh[/k] node and adjust the [k]Random Value[/k]'s Min input to see some craters get removed (Image 10). You can also increase the Subdivisions for the [k]Ico Sphere[/k] node to give the surface more faces (Image 11). Define a material and set it with a [k]Set Material[/k] node (Image 12).
